article.Citation/Title: Bogenschutz, M. P., Ross, S., Bhatt, S., Baron, T., Forcehimes, A. A., Laska, E., Mennenga, S. E., O'Donnell, K., Owens, L. T., Podrebarac, S., Rotrosen, J., Tonigan, J. S., & Worth, L. (2022). Percentage of heavy drinking days following psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy vs placebo in the treatment of adult patients with alcohol use disorder: A randomized clinical trial. JAMA Psychiatry, 79(10), 953-962.
article.InterventionDescription: Psilocybin 25-40 mg/70 kg (two 8-hour sessions, weeks 4 and 8) vs diphenhydramine 50-100 mg, alongside 12 sessions of manualized MET/CBT psychotherapy at two US academic centers.

ae_events.Description: One diphenhydramine-group participant had 2 psychiatric hospital admissions for suicidal ideation during binge-drinking episodes.
One diphenhydramine-group participant hospitalized for a Mallory-Weiss tear from severe vomiting during a binge-drinking episode.
Headache within 48h of dosing: 21/48 (43.8%) psilocybin vs 2/45 (4.4%) diphenhydramine participants.
Anxiety during psilocybin sessions, more frequent than diphenhydramine; 2 participants received oral diazepam 10mg, resolving in 45-210 min.
Nausea reported more frequently during psilocybin dosing sessions than diphenhydramine; no participant count given.
One psilocybin participant reported passive suicidal ideation for 15 minutes during dosing; resolved without sequelae.

article.Outcome: Primary outcome per abstract/Methods is percentage of heavy drinking days (PHDD), weeks 5-36, between-group. Efficacy section reports the between-group contrast directly as Hedges g = 0.52 (95% CI 0.11-0.94), mean difference 13.86 (95% CI 3.00-24.72), P=.01 (also Table 2, 'Between-group follow-up' row for %Heavy drinking days). Used the authors' own Hedges g rather than the mean-difference or the 3-dimensional MANOVA omnibus statistic, since g is the designated effect-size metric and requires no conversion.
article.SD: Paired F-test for the same PHDD weeks-5-36 between-group contrast is given in the Abstract as F(1,86)=6.43, P=.01, matching the P-value attached to the Hedges g in Table 2/Efficacy text. Note: the Results/Efficacy section separately reports F(1,86)=6.18, P=.02 for 'a main effect of treatment on the 3-dimensional drinking outcome vector' -- this is the multivariate MANOVA omnibus test across PHDD+PDD+DPD jointly, not the PHDD-specific univariate contrast, so it is a different statistic and was not used here. Flagging the two F-values as belonging to different analyses rather than treating them as inconsistent duplicates of the same number.
article.PVal: P=.01 printed exactly, attached to the same PHDD weeks-5-36 between-group Hedges g/mean-difference contrast (Abstract and Table 2).
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Table 2 gives the analyzed n for the between/within-group effect-size table as Diphenhydramine (n=45), Psilocybin (n=48); 45+48=93, matching 'Of the 95 randomized participants, 93 received at least 1 dose of study medication and were included in the primary outcome analysis.'

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Fully reported CONSORT-style RCT: explicit objective (Abstract/Intro), double-blind RCT design and 2-site setting named, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria, psilocybin vs diphenhydramine dosing/session structure, active comparator described, primary+secondary outcomes listed, a priori interim-analysis power plan (f2=0.16, power 0.8) plus post hoc power limitation discussed, randomization procedure (stratified blocks) and blinding procedure (with blinding-integrity data) both described, detailed statistical analysis plan, full Results section, dedicated Safety section with MedDRA-coded AE tabulation, and an extensive Funding/COI disclosure section.

article.Retention (%): Denominator = randomized N (95), since both randomized (95) and a broader 'qualified' pre-randomization pool (110) are reported, and attrition after randomization is what the criterion measures. Completers = participants who completed the full 8-month (32-week) double-blind follow-up per the CONSORT diagram: 42 (diphenhydramine) + 46 (psilocybin) = 88. 88/95 x 100 = 92.6%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Article reports non-Hispanic White = 78.9%; no single combined non-white figure is given. Computed as complement: 100 - 78.9 = 21.1. Note the article states race categories sum to >100% because 2 participants selected multiple categories, and Hispanic ethnicity (14.7%) is reported as a category alongside racial categories rather than crossed with them, so this 21.1% figure is an approximation using non-Hispanic-White as the reference 'majority' group, not a clean non-white sum.
article.BaseStatus: Judgment call. All participants met DSM-IV criteria for alcohol dependence (the more severe of DSM-IV's two AUD diagnoses), mean 5.3/7 dependence criteria, mean 14.2 years dependent, and WHO risk levels were Very High 31.6% / High 33.7% / Moderate 22.1% / Low 12.6% (majority high/very-high risk). Coded 'Severe' on this basis, despite the Discussion's own caveat that 'the study population was lower in drinking intensity at screening than in most AUD medication trials' -- that comment is a relative statement about comparability to other AUD pharmacotherapy trials, not an absolute severity description, and the dependence diagnosis plus risk-level distribution still indicate a severe target population.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Both sites are in the United States: New York University Grossman School of Medicine (New York, NY) and University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center (Albuquerque, NM).
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0. Although recruited from the community via advertisements, the funnel was highly selective (569 screened by phone -> 172 screened in person -> 110 qualified -> 95 randomized) with extensive psychiatric/medical exclusions (major psychiatric and drug use disorders, hallucinogen use, contraindicating medical conditions), consistent with a volunteer, highly-screened research sample rather than a real-world clinical/community population.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1. The primary MANOVA model included fixed effects for site and site-by-treatment interaction plus baseline covariates for each drinking measure; Discussion also substantively addresses inability to evaluate effects in subgroups (women, racial/ethnic minorities, psychiatric comorbidity) due to insufficient power, which is a substantive discussion of potential moderating factors.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 1. Table 1 reports household income as median (range): $100,000 ($3,700-$4,000,000). Although the median is not low, the reported range's floor ($3,700/year) documents that participants with very low income were part of the sample, and the field's own parenthetical ('income reported') treats explicit income reporting as sufficient evidence of SES description. This is a closer call than a study reporting only a low mean/median income (e.g., the field could instead be read as requiring evidence that low-SES participants specifically were included/targeted, which this article does not state as an eligibility criterion) -- flagged as a genuine judgment call.
article.Followup in months: Article defines its primary follow-up window as the '32-week double-blind period following the first dose of study medication' (weeks 5-36), consistent throughout Abstract, Methods, and Limitations ('does not provide information on the duration of effects beyond the 32-week double-blind observation period'). Converted using the stated weeks/4 convention: 32/4 = 8 months. A separate open-label extension (week 38 dosing + 18 more weeks) is described but is outside the double-blind results this article reports, so it was not used as the follow-up horizon.
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 0. The article states that 'training, supervision, and fidelity monitoring procedures are described in the protocol' but no feasibility/acceptability/fidelity results are reported as a study outcome in this article (fidelity monitoring is a study-conduct procedure, not a reported outcome measure).
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 0. The MEQ (States of Consciousness Questionnaire/Mystical Experience Questionnaire) was used as a subjective-effects/process measure of the acute drug session, not as a mental-health outcome (depression, anxiety, PTSD, well-being); no such mental-health outcome scale is reported.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'pooled'. The headline safety figures (204 total AEs: 119 psilocybin, 85 diphenhydramine) and the 3 serious adverse events are reported across both treatment arms together, not psilocybin-arm-only, even though some specific AE types (e.g., headache) are also broken out by arm.
article.AE_denominator: Coded 93 (participants who received >=1 dose of study medication: 48 psilocybin + 45 diphenhydramine), matching the 32-week AE-reporting period 'following the first administration of study medication.' Note: the Methods state AEs were coded 'occurring after informed consent,' which could imply a denominator of 95 (all randomized/consented) rather than 93 (as-treated); flagging this as an alternative reading not resolved by the text provided.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Coded 'Not numbered'. The main text names 204 total AE events and describes several specific AE types in prose (headache, anxiety, nausea, passive suicidal ideation, psychiatric hospitalization, Mallory-Weiss tear), but the full MedDRA-coded distinct-type breakdown is in eTable 2a/2b of Supplement 2, which is not included in the converted text provided for this extraction, so the true total distinct-type count cannot be verified.
article.AE_scope_cardiovascular_exclusion: The 'Cardiovascular Effects' subsection (under 'Acute Effects', not 'Safety') reports psilocybin was associated with transient increases in systolic/diastolic blood pressure and heart rate during dosing, resolving by ~300-360 minutes, but states explicitly 'no participant reported symptoms or was treated for hypertension.' This is analyzed elsewhere as a formal continuous safety outcome ('Safety Outcomes' subsection, mixed models for BP/HR) rather than adjudicated as one of the 204 MedDRA-coded adverse events in the 'Safety' section. Because it is asymptomatic, untreated, and not counted among the tabulated AEs, it was not added as a distinct ae_events row (captured instead under PhysicalChangeMeasured=1); flagged here as a non-obvious inclusion/exclusion judgment.

ae_events.Bogenschutz 2022_AE01: Graded Severe with SeveritySource='author': this is one of the article's explicitly enumerated 'three serious adverse events'; inpatient psychiatric hospitalization independently meets the FDA hospitalization seriousness criterion. Onset coded 'delayed' since it occurred during the 32-week follow-up in association with binge-drinking episodes, not during or immediately after a dosing session (this participant was in the diphenhydramine arm).
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2022_AE02: Graded Severe with SeveritySource='author' as one of the article's three named SAEs; hospitalization meets FDA seriousness criterion. Onset coded 'delayed' for the same reason as AE01 (diphenhydramine-arm, follow-up-period event, not a dosing-session event).
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2022_AE03: NAffected reported as 21 (psilocybin-arm count, the intervention of interest for this review); the diphenhydramine-arm rate (2/45, 4.4%) is captured in Description rather than as a second NAffected value, since the field takes a single integer. Onset 'post-session-acute' per the article's own framing that this is drawn from 'treatment-emergent adverse events occurring within 48 hours of study drug administration' (eTable 2b). Defaulted to Mild consistent with the Discussion's group-level characterization of psilocybin AEs as 'mostly mild and self-limiting' and the absence of any reported intervention or hospitalization for headache specifically, but SeverityIndeterminate set to 'Y' because no headache-specific duration, resolution, or intervention detail is given -- only the group-level statement, which is a general signal rather than event-specific evidence.
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2022_AE04: AE_type 'both': anxiety during psilocybin dosing is expected challenging-experience phenomenology but was also coded as a MedDRA AE. Graded Moderate (not Mild) because the article documents that a subset (2 participants) required active pharmacological intervention (oral diazepam 10 mg) per rubric guidance that expected in-session distress is graded by intervention need, not intensity; the rubric's Moderate band explicitly includes 'benzodiazepine rescue.' No total anxiety case count is given (only 'more frequently' and the 2-participant diazepam subset), so NAffected='.'.
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2022_AE05: SeverityIndeterminate=Y: nausea is named only as 'reported more frequently' with no case-level detail (no count, no intervention/duration specific to nausea). Defaulted to Mild per rubric's under-specified-AE rule, informed by the Discussion's general statement that psilocybin AEs were 'mostly mild and self-limiting,' but flagged indeterminate because that statement is a group-level characterization, not nausea-specific evidence.
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2022_AE06: SeverityIndeterminate=Y: this is a genuinely close call. The severity rubric lists 'suicidal behavior/attempt' among PAT-specific events that are Severe by default, but this event is passive ideation (not behavior/attempt), lasted 15 minutes, required no intervention, resolved without sequelae, and was NOT included among the article's own list of three named serious adverse events (all of which were in the diphenhydramine arm) -- an implicit author judgment that this event did not meet their seriousness bar. Graded Moderate as a middle position that neither silently downgrades a suicidal-ideation event to Mild (risking understated harm) nor overrides the authors' own non-SAE classification by declaring it Severe; flagged for human review given the safety-sensitive nature of any suicidal ideation signal.

config_proposal.note: Authors report Hedges' g = 0.52 (95% CI 0.11-0.94) directly for the primary PHDD between-group contrast at weeks 5-36 (Table 2/Efficacy text); this is a direct pass-through of an author-computed Hedges g, no conversion required. Article's own convention already orients positive g toward the favored (psilocybin) direction, so direction=1.
